text:
Sanjay: quick q — trying to bring up zeppelin-9b for a paid POC. license in the repo looks research-only. can we serve to a customer under Dedicated or Private? link: https://hf.co/zeppelin/9b
Emma: short answer probably not without vendor ok. what's the exact language?
Li: pasted the key bits I found:
```
"""
Zeppelin License v0.9 excerpt:
- Use permitted for non-commercial research only.
- Redistribution of weights, checkpoints, or derivative models is prohibited.
- Hosting the model as a service or offering access to third parties is disallowed unless a commercial license is obtained.
- Attribution to the Zeppelin research group required in published outputs.
"""
```
Maya: so two things to check: 1) does a customer POC count as "commercial"? 2) are quantized weights / compiled kernels considered "derivatives"?
Courtney (Legal): yes to both in most cases. if the customer is paying or we're providing a customer-facing endpoint, it's commercial. quantized/converted weights are usually treated as derivative works — still covered by the license. an NDA with the customer doesn't change the license terms.
Sanjay: ugh. we already started perf/quant experiments locally. no weights left the infra, but the POC would expose the model via api to their account.
Emma: operationally we could run the POC on Private (VPC) and restrict network, but that doesn't address the "hosting/as-a-service" clause.
Courtney (Legal): correct. Some licenses explicitly ban "hosted service" even if it's private. Options: request a commercial/POC license from the authors, choose a different model, or get a written permission to host for a time-limited POC. I'll draft vendor language.
Maya: another thing — the excerpt mentions required attribution. if vendor permits hosting, they'll probably require an attribution string in the UI and in any published results. make sure product can show that.
Li: infra note: quantized artifacts still count as the model in most legal interpretations. we can't ship them to customers or to a marketplace.
Sanjay: can we instead produce canned outputs (like precomputed responses) and serve those? would that avoid hosting?
Courtney (Legal): maybe for a demo, but if the customer interacts dynamically it's effectively hosting. precomputed static examples are safe for a demo. dynamic access -> need license.
Emma: also check for any share-alike / copyleft bits — if they force us to open-source derivatives that's a non-starter for product.
Courtney (Legal): noted. I'll flag share-alike as deal-breaker in vendor conversation.
Sanjay: plan: 1) pause any external-facing deploys 2) run internal eval + benchmarks only 3) Courtney will reach out to authors for a POC/commercial clause 4) if denied, pick alternate model.
Maya: thanks. please paste the license file into the ticket so legal has the canonical text.
Courtney (Legal): will do. drafting now, aim to send today. cc @Maya @Emma
Deploy Bot: perf test (quantized local): p50 48ms, p95 120ms on a8g, logs: https://internal/redwood/logs/1715567890-zeppelin-eval
Sanjay: thanks all. I'll open the vendor-ticket and attach evals. will update thread when vendor replies. :+1:
